extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists (Royal Society members and readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards for writing and reporting experimental natural-philosophy observations, laboratory chemistry experiments, clinical case reports, and field observations as exemplified in Philosophical Transactions articles. Emphasizes precise measurement, reproducible procedure, observational detail, and situating results in prior experience and literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground claims in experience and reproducible observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims or general suppositions must be tested against experience; if contrary to experience they should be refuted or reconsidered (e.g., 'this he refutes, as contrary to experience' regarding acids from fermentations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical counterexamples or repeated observations that either support or contradict the asserted generalization; do not rely solely on speculative reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explicit experimental procedures and demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He demands an experiment how to make an acidum ex sale alkali.' — when asserting a chemical transformation, give a concrete method to effect and demonstrate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the steps, reactants, and manipulations clearly enough that others can repeat the transformation; include reagents, conditions, and any preparatory steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish and define chemical entities precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid confounding different classes of substances (e.g., 'he confounds salia alkalia et acida; for they must needs differ in their natures').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear definitions and properties of acids, alkalis, oils, salts, etc., and show with experiments how they differ (e.g., effervescence on mixture, solubility, reactions with metals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use counterexamples and alternative hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Test a hypothesis by citing or producing contrary cases (e.g., wines which ferment very high without acidity to rebut 'all fermentations produce acids').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek counterinstances; when presenting a general rule, address known exceptions and explain them (ex. 'follows fermentation ex accidenti ratione materiae').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report instruments, reference points, and precise positional data for astronomical observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comet observations include exact dates, longitudes, latitudes, and comparison with known stars ('the comet appeared in the telescope along with the star in virgo marked 11 by Bayer', 'arcturus was seen through the telescope along with the comet').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give date (new/old style), celestial coordinates, reference stars, and mention the instrument (telescope) and any known alignment or calibration details so others can verify or recalculate positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record full clinical case chronology and observable signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Case report of hydrophobia gives timeline of bite, onset of symptoms, sequence of signs (pains, paralysis, pulse intermission), treatments given (purging spirit, bleeding), and outcome (death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide dates/timing, sequence of symptoms, physical findings (pulse, temperature, appearance), interventions and doses where possible, observed responses, and post hoc interpretations (e.g., likely paralytic origin of symptoms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeted field tests and direct observation to infer causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Boiling fountains: digging nearby, pouring water on dry ground to reproduce bubbling, placing light bodies at vent mouths, and applying flame to test inflammability of emitted vapour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the field manipulations used to isolate causal factors and the observed outcomes; report negative as well as positive tests (e.g., vapour did not flame with a candle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe measurement apparatus, calibration, and method details for weighing and specific gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Weights of a cubic foot of bodies were measured 'in a vessel of well-seasoned Oak, whose Concave was an exact Cubic Foot'; scales sensitivity (turning with 2 ounces or 1 ounce) and avoirdupois units are stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify container geometry, calibration standards, scale sensitivity, units used, and whether solids/fluid methods differ (hydrostatic weighing in air & water vs equal-portion weighing in a glass).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain calculation methods and how to use tabulated data
rubrics_metrics.description: After listing weights and proportional specific gravities, the text explains using the 'rule of three' to find the weight of a cubic foot of a body from its proportion to water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompany tables with instructions for computation and examples showing how readers can apply the data to derive weights or magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose errors, repeat trials, and reliability of measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Author notes 'the last 4 observations may require some better calculation, as an error of some minutes seems to have crept in' and identifies which quicksilver measurement is 'more to be depended on.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected errors, differences between trials, which trials are considered more reliable and why, and any corrections or cautions for data users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situate observations within prior literature and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors cite previous writers and correspondents (Varenius, Plott, Erasmus Bartholinus, letters to/from Ciampini) and compare observations across regions (Peroul, Wigan, Japan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references to prior observations, acknowledge related reports, and discuss how new findings confirm, extend, or contradict existing accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record standardized weather variables daily and visualize barometer changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation of a printed list for every day with the barometer mapped by parallel lines and daily entries of wind quarter, rain/fair, frost/snow, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect daily, standardized meteorological entries and employ consistent visualization or mapping (e.g., Lister's parallel-line barometer chart) to detect patterns over years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflating theoretical causes; link phenomena to distinct principles with supporting experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Debates about whether heat/flammability arise from 'oleum' vs 'acidum et urinosum' stress that distinct principles should not be confounded and must be supported by experimental examples (e.g., oil of vitriol behavior, calx viva producing heat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing causal principles, show experiments that differentiate them (e.g., mixing tests, dissolution of metals, ignition behavior), and explain why alternative explanations are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify composition, state, and handling conditions for reactive mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of fulminating gold and burning mixtures notes the importance of dryness/imbibition and whether precipitates have been dried or imbibed (e.g., 'if the precipitate should be dried, and imbibed sometimes with a spirit of urine, it will then recover its fulminating power').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting reactive or explosive combinations, list exact components, their proportions, physical state (dry/wet), and any preparatory or storage conditions that affect behavior (drying, impregnation).
